chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A man fasted for a day, not knowing whether it was from the month of Ramadan or from another month. Then a group of people came and testified that it was from the month of Ramadan. Some people said, "According to us, it is not accepted."' He said, 'Yes, it is accepted.' I said, 'They say: You fasted while you did not know if this was from the month of Ramadan or from another.' He said, 'Yes, count it.'

For indeed, it is something God has guided you to. Indeed, the day of doubt should be fasted as being from Sha'ban and not as being from the month of Ramadan, because it is forbidden that a person act alone in fasting on the day of doubt. Rather, he should make the intention from the night before that he is fasting from Sha'ban. So if it turns out to be from the month of Ramadan, it suffices for him through the grace of God the Exalted and by what He has eased upon His servants — and had it not been for that, the people would have been destroyed.

key_terms.بتفضل الله: By the grace/favor of God — highlighting divine leniency when acts are done in good faith
key_terms.لا ينفرد: Acting alone/unilaterally — referring to the prohibition of independently declaring the start of Ramadan without communal verification
key_terms.يوم الشك: The Day of Doubt (Yawm al-Shakk): the 30th of Sha'ban when there is uncertainty about the start of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: If a person fasts on the Day of Doubt without knowing it is Ramadan, does their fast count?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the jurisprudential ruling regarding fasting on Yawm al-Shakk — the 'Day of Doubt' — which is the thirtieth of Sha'ban when it is uncertain whether Ramadan has commenced. The Imam rules that such a fast, if made with the intention of Sha'ban (not Ramadan), is retroactively validated as a Ramadan fast if witnesses later confirm the month had begun, through God's grace. He emphasizes that one is forbidden to fast the day of doubt with the intention that it is Ramadan, and that divine mercy accommodates genuine uncertainty, preventing undue hardship upon believers.
